thread.title: Oil Bulls Trampled, Stocks Wobble; Chip Stock Rallies | Investor's Business Daily

author: DAVID SAITO-CHUNG
title: Oil Bulls Trampled, Stocks Wobble; Chip Stock Rallies | Investor's Business Daily
text:
Big seesawing action by Apple ( AAPL ) pretty much defined the movement in U.S. stocks today . At one point, the Nasdaq composite gave back all of a 1.7% early advance. Crude oil plunged more than 8% to reach a session low of $54.91 a barrel and hit its lowest levels since December of last year.
X At 7218, the Nasdaq traded fractionally higher. Overall, the leading index for growth stocks is not making much of a rebound after falling a combined 4.9% in the prior three days of heavy selling. The Nasdaq remains well beneath its 50- and 200-day moving averages despite an important Day 7 follow-through that took place last week.
The Dow Jones industrial average slipped around 0.5% on the back of declines of 1 point or more by at least six of its 30 components. The S&P 500 traded near break-even.
Strength in building, RV, auto, home furnishings, fabless semiconductor, gaming and airline stocks offset big declines in oil, meat, home medical care, medical services, hospital and beverage shares.
The Russell 2000 slipped 0.3%.
Income Plays Still Prevail Investors continued to hunt for yield. The Dow utility average rallied 0.5%.
Mortgage REIT Arbor Realty Trust ( ABR ) gained more than 1.5% to 12.66 in heavy volume. Shares moved further past a 12.45 proper buy point in a nearly 10-week flat base and remain in the proper buy zone .
Arbor had recently carved out a spot in the IBD 50. Other REITs making the list include Medical Properties Trust ( MPW ) and Caesars casino operator and hospitality services play Vici Properties ( VICI ).
Arbor's revenue has increased 143%, 40%, 18%, 31%, 34% and 37% vs. year-ago levels in the past six quarters. Arbor, based in Uniondale, N.Y., sports an 8% annualized dividend yield. The S&P 500 has a yield of less than 1.9%.
Intel Strengthens, Home Depot Wild Within the 30-stock Dow industrials, Intel ( INTC ) gained nearly 2% and is trying to snap a two-day selling streak. Shares in the semiconductor giant recently climbed back above the 50-day moving average, a bullish sign. The stock is still 17% below a 52-week high of 57.60.
Intel clearly needs more time to work on a new base .
The stock's RS Rating has improved from 40 to 59 in the past four weeks.
Home Depot ( HD ) traded wildly but pushed well into the upper half of the day's trading range. The DIY home improvement retail chain posted a 36% jump in fiscal third-quarter profit to $2.51 a share as sales increased 5%.
Home Depot cleared a 204.35 buy point in a shallow cup with handle in September but did not go very far. Gains of 5% soon vanished as the October market correction took hold.
Inside The IBD 50 Within the IBD 50 , mountain bike and ATV suspension components supplier Fox Factory ( FOXF ) rallied as much as 4%, briefly hitting the 70 level for the first time in four trading days. Last week, the stock rushed past a 73.20 buy point in a V-shaped cup base.
V-shaped patterns have a history of failing because their quick move up from the bottom of the base tends to spark heavy profit-taking as the stock hits new highs.
Watch for the stock to potentially form a handle or create a new base next to the six-week cup without handle.
Fox Factory ranks No. 5 within the IBD 50 .
In Other Financial Markets Investors continued to seek a haven in government bonds. The yield on the benchmark U.S. Treasury 10-year note sank 4 basis points to 3.14%.
President Trump's criticism of Saudi Arabia's plan to cut output helped spark a big sell-off in crude oil prices. WTI futures plunged more than 6% and slumped below $56 a barrel. Yet natural gas futures soared. The near-term contract hit as high as $4.09 per million BTU and notched the highest levels since late 2014.
